chunk_findings.detail: With `[lease].reconcile_tests` at its specified default `affected`, a complete is cleared by any post-`at` `unit_tests` or `ci` pass whose `evidence.tree_sha` merely starts with the 12-char main prefix. The knob text in `knob_added.lease.reconcile_tests.toml` defines `affected` as the tests the reconciled files select, and the governing note refuses complete until those affected tests passed on the reconciled tree. Given `reconciled={files:["pkg/a.py"], main:"abcdef0123456789", at:"2026-10-17T00:00:00Z"}` and a `ci` pass at a later stamp with `tree_sha="abcdef012345+clean"` and no file selection, line 332 sets `passed` and the function returns `""`, so complete proceeds even though the affected tests for `pkg/a.py` never ran. The inverse is also wrong: a gate that did run only the tests selected by `pkg/a.py` is never consulted, so that pass cannot clear the guard. The refusal string always tells the operator to run `unit_tests`, which is the full suite, not the affected set.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion/rules.py:330

chunk_findings.detail: The required evidence is a suite run that names the reconciled files. `names_reconciled_tree` ignores every evidence field except `tree_sha`, and the comment states the note is never consulted. Given `reconciled.files=["src/lease.py"]` and a `unit_tests` PASSED record at or after `at` whose evidence is only `{tree_sha: "<main-prefix>+clean"}` with no reconciled path, `passed_on_reconciled_tree` is true and `_reconciled_blocker` returns `""`, so complete is allowed without evidence naming `src/lease.py`.

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_reconciled_merge_with_a_passed_ci_completes` clears the reconcile blocker for a `ci` pass whose evidence is only the prose `affected tests on the reconciled tree: tests/test_x.py (reached by src/x.py)`. That string does not name the reconciled commit (`base`/`main` are HEAD). The governing note requires the affected tests to have passed on the reconciled tree, and the later tests in this file reject path-substring notes and `tree_sha` values that do not start with the reconciled SHA. Given that evidence, this test requires the guard to drop, so a pre-reconcile run whose note merely mentions `src/x.py` is accepted as proof.

chunk_findings.detail: The lease filter was removed, so autoformat still stages files outside the item's globs. Previously `owned` kept only paths matching `it.globs`. Now it is every path from `changed_python(..., own=True)`. Three-dot only drops files `base` introduced; it does not enforce the lease. Given an item whose globs are `src/a.py` and a commit that also edits unformatted `src/b.py`, `base...sha` returns both, `auto_fix` rewrites and stages `src/b.py`, and the outside-lease collision this bug names still happens.

chunk_findings.detail: The replacement test never runs the hook, so it does not lock the stated regression. It only asserts `changed_python(own=True) == ["src/a.py"]` on a throwaway repo. It does not call `cirun.run` / `auto_fix`, and it never checks that an unformatted file outside the item's changes is left unstaged. A hook that still formats and stages `src/b.py` (the old glob case, or any path that ignores `owned`) passes this test.

chunk_findings.detail: The help and docstring promise a diff/plan mode that reports what `refresh_docs` would rewrite, but nothing here computes a diff or compares content. `_plan_driver` at least classifies create/current/refuse/rewrite; `_plan_block` reads `existing` and is passed `section`, then ignores both and always returns "would refresh the managed block in {label}". `_plan_native` never opens the rule file and always returns "would refresh the native rule for {key}". Given an adopted repo whose AGENTS.md managed block already equals `section`, and a native rule that already matches the template, `refresh_docs(..., plan=True)` still lists both as refreshes and shows none of the bytes that a hand-edited driver would lose to `.local-edits`. An operator cannot tell a no-op from the B420810120e clobber, which is the case this mode was added to preview.

chunk_findings.detail: The new early return classifies a missing rules file as an append, which contradicts both the docstring and the empty-file branch a few lines later. Given a FORM_BLOCK native rule whose path does not exist, `_plan_native` calls `_plan_block` and line 186 returns "would append the managed block to {label}" without ever reading content. The same function treats a present but empty file (`NO_BLOCK` and `not existing.strip()`) as "would create {label}". `--plan` therefore tells the operator an existing file will be appended to when adopt would create the file, so the plan mode this change adds still mis-reports the write.

chunk_findings.detail: The new early return classifies a missing rules file as an append, which contradicts both the docstring and the empty-file branch a few lines later. Given a FORM_BLOCK native rule whose path does not exist, `_plan_native` calls `_plan_block` and line 186 returns "would append the managed block to {label}" without ever reading content. The same function treats a present but empty file (`NO_BLOCK` and `not existing.strip()`) as "would create {label}". `--plan` therefore tells the operator an existing file will be appended to when adopt would create the file, so the plan mode this change adds still mis-reports the write.

chunk_findings.detail: The help and docstring promise a diff/plan mode that reports what `refresh_docs` would rewrite, but nothing here computes a diff or compares content. `_plan_driver` at least classifies create/current/refuse/rewrite; `_plan_block` reads `existing` and is passed `section`, then ignores both and always returns "would refresh the managed block in {label}". `_plan_native` never opens the rule file and always returns "would refresh the native rule for {key}". Given an adopted repo whose AGENTS.md managed block already equals `section`, and a native rule that already matches the template, `refresh_docs(..., plan=True)` still lists both as refreshes and shows none of the bytes that a hand-edited driver would lose to `.local-edits`.
